question.problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+xy+2x+y$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,-1).$
question.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,-1)$, can be found by computing $∇f(1,-1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+xy+2x+y)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+xy+2x+y)\text{ }j \\  & =(2x+y+2)\text{ }i+(-2y+x+1)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(1,-1) & =(2(1)+(-1)+2)\text{ }i+(-2(-1)+1+1)\text{ }j \\  & =3\,i+4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(1,-1)}{‖∇f(1,-1)‖} & =\frac{3\,i+4\,j}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{5}(3\,i+4\,j)\end{aligned}
$$
